title: the launch tool's proof reads its child's cgroup through the cgroup tool
intention: The launch tool's scoped-exec tooth reads the child's own cgroup through cairn.tools.cgroup.cgroup.cgroup_of, so cairn/tools/cgroup/cgroup.py stays the one python reader of /proc/<pid>/cgroup and the ground loop's one-reader tooth reads green.
why: Measured 2026-11-23 on akiendelllinux: cairn/devices/recovery/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py reds 'exactly one file READS /proc/<pid>/cgroup from python', readers [cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/proofs/test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py, cairn/tools/cgroup/cgroup.py, cairn/tools/cgroup/proofs/test_cgroup.py]. 60f16ffccd43 (PROVED; red-first proof sealed b3c17da82, 2026-11-22) wrote _READ_MAX, a one-liner that opens /proc/self/cgroup with read_text() inside the scoped child. No ticket names the red (grep of tickets and questions for the proof name and the tooth's words). Under Law 9 being on main earlier exempts nothing.
traces_to: Law 9 (a red on main carries a ticket) and Law 1 (the cgroup parse is settled once in cairn/tools/cgroup; re-deriving it in a proof is the defect the one-reader tooth guards).
how: Rewrite _READ_MAX in the launch proof so the scoped child puts the repo root on sys.path, imports cgroup_of from cairn.tools.cgroup.cgroup, and prints memory.max from /sys/fs/cgroup + cgroup_of('self'); tooth 3's assertion is unchanged. The ground loop proof is unchanged and goes green.

clauses.claim: cairn/devices/recovery/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py arm six reads green: the python readers of /proc/<pid>/cgroup are cairn/tools/cgroup/cgroup.py and its own proof only
the launch proof's scoped-exec tooth still needs the child's memory.max to equal 100M, read through cgroup_of

decisions.text: D1: in cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/proofs/test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py, _READ_MAX becomes a child that inserts the repo root on sys.path, imports cgroup_of from cairn.tools.cgroup.cgroup, and prints 'memory.max' and the text of /sys/fs/cgroup<cgroup_of('self')>/memory.max; test_a_scoped_exec_runs_under_the_memory_max_passed passes the repo root into it as it already does for the launch import. No other line changes; its seal is resealed in the build.

constraints: the ground loop proof's one-reader tooth is not weakened, widened or given a declared exemption for this file
the launch proof still measures the kernel's memory.max, not the tool's word for it
